title: Multi-tenant isolation overview (SaaS on AWS)
hook: Software as a Service (SaaS) means many customers share your platform. On AWS you isolate tenants by silo (account per tenant), pool (shared stack with row-level separation), or bridge (hybrid) — each trades cost against blast radius.

blocks.text: Multi-tenancy is an architecture pattern where one deployment serves multiple customers (tenants). AWS SaaS patterns classify isolation models: silo deploys dedicated resources per tenant (separate accounts or stacks), pool shares compute and database with tenant_id discrimination, bridge mixes pooled app tier with siloed data for premium tenants. Identity routing — subdomain, JWT claim, or API key — maps requests to the correct tenant context at the application layer.

entries.plainDefinition: A customer organization whose data and configuration must be isolated from others.
Dedicated infrastructure per tenant — strongest isolation, highest cost.
entries.example: Separate RDS instance per enterprise customer.

entries.plainDefinition: Shared application and database with logical separation via tenant key.
entries.example: Single DynamoDB table with partition key tenantId.

entries.plainDefinition: One tenant's load degrades performance for others in a pooled stack.
entries.example: Heavy batch job from tenant A slows API for tenant B.

blocks.text: FAANG and B2B SaaS interviews ask how you prevent cross-tenant data leaks. AWS provides account and IAM boundaries, but application code must enforce tenant_id on every query. A missing WHERE tenant_id = ? clause in pooled RDS is a headline breach. Premium tiers often justify silo or bridge models for compliance (HIPAA, SOC 2).

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Name silo vs pool tradeoff, then explain how you enforce tenant context in app layer and IAM — AWS does not auto-isolate pooled rows.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Tenant resolution
items.body: Extract tenant from subdomain, JWT claim, or API key at API Gateway or ALB.

items.title: Context propagation
items.body: Pass tenant_id through middleware to every database query and cache key.

items.title: Authorization check
items.body: Verify user belongs to resolved tenant before any data access.

items.title: Audit
items.body: Log tenant_id on every mutation for forensics and compliance.

snippet.label: CloudFormation: per-tenant S3 prefix policy with ABAC
snippet.code:
Policies:
  - PolicyName: TenantScopedS3
    PolicyDocument:
      Version: '2012-10-17'
      Statement:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action: s3:GetObject
          Resource: arn:aws:s3:::saas-uploads/${aws:PrincipalTag/tenantId}/*
          Condition:
            StringEquals:
              aws:ResourceTag/tenantId: '${aws:PrincipalTag/tenantId}'
snippet.explanation: Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) scopes S3 access to the tenant tag on the principal — IAM enforces isolation at storage layer.

snippet.label: CLI: provision silo account via Organizations
snippet.code:
aws organizations create-account \
  --email tenant-acme@company.internal \
  --account-name tenant-acme-prod

aws organizations move-account \
  --account-id 333333333333 \
  --source-parent-id r-root \
  --destination-parent-id ou-tenants-silo
snippet.explanation: Silo model: dedicated account per premium tenant under a Tenants OU with tailored SCPs.

snippet.label: CloudFormation: DynamoDB pooled table design
snippet.code:
Resources:
  TenantDataTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: tenantId
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: itemId
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: tenantId
          KeyType: HASH
        - AttributeName: itemId
          KeyType: RANGE
snippet.explanation: Partition key tenantId isolates data at storage engine level — every query must include tenantId.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Trusting client-supplied tenant_id without server-side verification. Shared Redis cache keys without tenant prefix. Running pooled and silo tenants on the same IAM role without ABAC conditions.

blocks.text: Tenant isolation is defense in depth: routing layer resolves tenant, middleware enforces membership, data layer scopes every query, IAM ABAC scopes object storage, and audit logs correlate tenant_id. Pen tests focus on IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) — changing tenantId in a JWT or URL. How to prove it in production: integration tests that attempt cross-tenant reads, CloudTrail data events on tenant buckets, and per-tenant rate limits at API Gateway to mitigate noisy neighbor.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: High if app bug — one missing filter
N stacks or accounts to patch
Need rate limits and fair scheduling

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'we use separate databases so we are multi-tenant safe' without explaining request routing and authorization — or claiming pooled RDS is secure without row-level enforcement and integration tests for cross-tenant access.

interviewTakeaways: Multi-tenant SaaS uses silo, pool, or bridge models — trade isolation against cost and ops burden.
AWS provides account and IAM boundaries; application code must enforce tenant_id on every data path.
ABAC with principal tags, DynamoDB partition keys, and rate limits are production patterns for pooled SaaS.
60s: Silo = account/stack per tenant. Pool = shared with tenant_id everywhere. Bridge = hybrid tiers. Defense in depth: routing, authz, query scope, IAM, audit. Test IDOR.
Follow-up: how would you migrate a pooled tenant to silo for an enterprise deal?
commonPitfalls: Accepting tenant_id from the client without binding to authenticated user — saying pooled RDS is enough gets you rejected.
Strong answer: resolve tenant server-side, enforce on every query, ABAC on S3, integration tests for cross-tenant reads.
Cache keys without tenant prefix causing data bleed between customers.
Single IAM role for all tenants without session tags or resource conditions.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Attach tenantId to AsyncLocalStorage or request context after JWT validation — every repository method reads from context, never from req.body.tenantId alone.
Lambda authorizer returns IAM policy with principalId and context map — pass tenantId as context for downstream Lambda without re-parsing JWT in every function.
